program.sourceCorrespondence: Independently rechecked producer evidence; public hashes alone do not certify source truth.

algorithm.allocationMapping: Retain all input identities. Map new core identities in allocation order to the first unused oN identity. Preserve aliases and ECMAScript own-key order.

detail.meaning: Direct V8 detail codec over version-neutral typed selected transitions; no legacy wire conversion.

logicalTest.decision: Boolean derived only from the current operand: && tests falsiness, || tests truthiness, ?? tests non-nullishness. No future right operand is included.

protocol.meaning: Checked Symbol identities, descriptors, receiver-aware access, scoped calls, construction, iterators, ordinary enumeration, generators, Number and PropertyKey conversion, Promise joins and executors, Proxy traps and binary memory in the same authoritative heap.

lifecycle.mixedReceipts: Intent result sequence and owner sequence refer to the mixed public timeline and its owner track. Unjournaled native arrivals are absent from causal contexts.
lifecycle.recovery: Replay acknowledged lifecycle records; restored dispatched work is uncertain and is never redispatched without explicit reconciliation.

protocolState.heap: Existing heap nodes with property, descriptor and private-element Maps serialized as entry arrays; Symbol keys remain tagged pairs.

asyncCalls.storage: Retained asyncCall metadata belongs to its internal execution Promise; asyncFunction marks its callable closure.
asyncCalls.capabilities: First await detaches the child and restores its caller scope. Later continuations resume in the realm FIFO with the same receiver, live capture cells, and execution Promise. Child completion settles that Promise without completing its parent invocation.
asyncCalls.boundaries: Async Promise callbacks, Promise adoption, thenable assimilation and implicit scheduler completion require separate profiles.

construction.sourceCallables: Explicit function source offsets and source-inventoried class:<offset>:constructor|instance|static bodies.
construction.continuations: Owned base/derived constructor receivers, newTarget, field initializers and captured superclass selection; private fields and methods retain declaring-class identities.

iterators.capabilities: Builtin array keys/values/entries and Unicode string iteration, live array length, sticky exhaustion and explicit result/pair allocation identities.

ordinaryCompletions.capabilities: Ordinary synchronous catch/finally scopes retain pending completion and bounded loop target identities. Break and continue targets belong to the same frame; only loop targets permit continue. Source qualification privately checks destinations without publishing bytecode.

customIteration.capabilities: Ordinary synchronous custom for-of and flat variable array bindings use checked properties, cached next and receiver cells, scoped calls, and ordinary cleanup. Independent observations check acquisition, done/value reads, and IteratorClose order and precedence.
customIteration.boundaries: Malformed intrinsic TypeErrors, asynchronous iteration, and nested or assignment pattern source projection require separate qualification; runtime execution alone does not admit them.

enumeration.capabilities: Stable ordinary for-in snapshots preserve own-key order, prototype walks, nonenumerable shadowing and fresh per-step result identities. Value writes are live; changed key/prototype structure is refused on the next step.

promiseJoins.capabilities: Invocation-owned Promise joins share the realm heap. A settlement publishes eligible dependencies across all retained invocations in registration order; an explicit queueMicrotask preserves enqueue order. Steps require the realm FIFO head and no competing active turn. First settlement and explicit late no-op steps preserve result identity. allSettled allocates one distinct ordinary status/value-or-reason object per input reaction, waits for every input and preserves input order and value aliases. Entries become ordinary mutable guest objects after fulfillment. Collecting joins reserve one array property for length.

faults.symbol-to-number: Cannot convert a Symbol value to a number
faults.ordinary-exhausted: Cannot convert object to primitive value

primitiveConversions.capabilities: Goal-derived live method order and hint, retained getter results, shared nested callback scopes, original abrupt identities, bounded ordinary builtin leaves and checked scalar conversion.
primitiveConversions.boundaries: Intrinsic fault records are independently derived by replay; original-source admission still refuses them until its complete fault observation authority is qualified. Proxy conversion, dynamic builtin callbacks, compound/logical/update object keys and unbounded stringification remain explicit refusals.

numberConversions.capabilities: Live data-method selection, original receiver and number hint, shared callback scopes, ordered ordinary fallback and checked primitive conversion. Synchronous callback throws preserve their completion through catch/finally and suppress fallback. Accessor selection, intrinsic TypeErrors and exotic conversion remain separate profiles.

generators.capabilities: Retained invocations, receivers, arguments and captures; sent values, catch/finally cleanup, suspension and cached-next delegation through declared builtin iterators and synchronous generators.

proxyCalls.capabilities: Distinct Proxy, target and handler identities; ordinary data forwarding and synchronous owned get/set traps with live target invariants and exact pending callback completion. Callable or revoked proxies and other traps require explicit profiles.

promiseExecutors.capabilities: Synchronous source executor calls, stable resolving function identities, a shared first-call cell, retained resolvers, primitive or owned Promise resolution, and executor throw rejection. Thenables, self resolution and async executor bodies require separate profiles.

binaryMemory.capabilities: Fixed ordinary buffers and fixed/growable shared buffers; scalar conversions; shared view identities; bounded single-agent atomic operations. No detach, transfer, host buffers or cross-agent scheduling.

protocolState.lifecycle: Protocol and ordinary detail share retained invocations, heap, locals and realm scheduler. Host requests, callbacks and observed results use the same checked lifecycle. Declared catch/finally, loop cleanup and Promise scheduler detail retain their independent profile boundaries. Join steps require an empty stack, the globally next ready owner and the owning invocation.

ingressLogReceipt.meaning: Private write-ahead arrival chain head. Each registered or return-value callback arrival is captured before yielding, persisted and read back before queue mutation or delivery. Checkpoints refuse unresolved/failed writes and retain their acknowledged head. Restore requires an independently retained equal or later head; validates every source, public prefix, graph and arrival order before applying absent inputs. Delivered/discarded inputs are reconciled without redispatch; a later public boundary than the checkpoint refuses.

callbackArrival.meaning: Private return-value callback input bound to its original source, public prefix, supplied closure/captures and committed external parent. Receiver and arguments share one alias-preserving graph; introduced objects cannot overwrite retained identities. Queued arrivals reconstruct from the independent journal with shared registered-event/callback FIFO. Active and completed children must match public history. Neither an adapter Promise nor an external parent result is reconstructed or inferred.

ingressReceipt.meaning: Private reference to immutable canonical pending-ingress snapshot bytes. Its SHA-256 content digest checks integrity against an independently retained expected receipt; it is not broker authentication.

ingressSnapshot.meaning: Private, bounded registered-event inputs bound to one exact public prefix and source-owned handler. Monotonic arrival sequences preserve eligible callback order within a retained realm; different realms remain independent. The sequence cursor and event graphs never enter model context.

checkpoint.ingressCursor: Private next host-event arrival sequence, persisted in generic selected-state and region checkpoints even when no pending snapshot is present.

protocolSelected.meaning: Exact shared states, activation statuses and host policy are independently reconstructed from the complete public V8 history. Pending registered events require the separately retained private ingress receipt and snapshot. Queued return-value callbacks require their independently retained journal and exact original input/parent binding. Pending unjournaled native ingress refuses checkpoint creation. Restore marks acknowledged outstanding work uncertain and existing subscriptions lost; only explicitly supplied services and reattachment may recover them. Completed callback return/throw is available for explicit parent reconciliation without recreating adapter continuations or redispatching effects.

checkpoint.restore: Validate public mixed replay and exact shared state. Restore existing intent/handler lifecycle without invoking adapters.

supervision.generated: Only exact generated semantic line bytes and framing EOS.
supervision.observed: Definitions, entry envelopes, inputs, dispatch receipts and external results have zero prediction loss.
supervision.private: Source archives, correspondence maps, future observations, reference outcomes and receipt sidecars never enter prompts.

promotion.tokenizer: exact serialized input and whole-sequence encoding required
promotion.model: external results or explicit untested disposition
promotion.default: not promoted by engineering receipts alone

fixtures.reason: old artifacts require their original contract
